groups.title: Standing hypotheses and equation scope
groups.source_reader_scope: BMP on X and positive lower volume of an ordinary model phi bound masses in E_phi; phi need not admit a smaller-background envelope. General finite data yield relative-class membership, while Lp data give the ordinary type. Positive exponent fixes potentials; at zero only the scalar is unique.

groups.title: Fixed finite measure and common rooftops
groups.source_reader_scope: Disjoint first-contact pieces avoid an obstacle-count factor. The ell lower bound replaces kappa in the preceding chapter, stretched tails and finite-prefix competitors give all relative-class tests, and weighted lsc plus zero domination yield capacity and weak-measure continuity.

groups.title: Relative moments and self-measure error
groups.source_reader_scope: Choose w prime of the same ordinary type as the fixed reference w with mass exceeding M-ell/2. The maximum estimate and moment tails prevent collapse and rule out empty stretching envelopes. The positive-part variant uses rooftops; summable self-measure error gives all tail rooftops and convergence in capacity.

groups.title: Concave envelopes and higher moments
groups.source_reader_scope: In the ordinary minimal type, a strict analytic barrier gives a locally bounded locus; inverse convex composition gives contact domination. The adapted distribution weight uses N=2n+1, r=1+1/(4N), ell_V and M_V; the uniform Lr bound concerns V-u, with V itself only fixed L1(nu).

groups.title: Minimal-reference general equations
groups.source_reader_scope: Coordinate convolution with finite A_theta, uniform first moments, higher uniform integrability and moving integral estimates give capacity and measure convergence. Bounded-carrier density truncations handle arbitrary finite non-pluripolar measures in E_V, without asserting ordinary minimal type. BMP plus metric positive lower mass gives positive lower volume for every big background.

groups.title: Cross-class projection and moving models
groups.source_reader_scope: Small stretches of phi against the upper model eta and arbitrary stretches of z combine into a rooftop competitor with volume approaching that of phi. Projection is in E_phi and only retains the contact measure. Varying models require a common delta lower bound and d_theta convergence; restricted domination gives class closure, and global finite domination gives capacity/weak-measure limits.

groups.title: Weighted approximation limits
groups.source_reader_scope: A common E_phi lower bound, not an ordinary-type condition on the approximants, gives convergence in capacity from a weighted error. In truncated addition the discarded region decays exponentially under uniform finite input masses. Cutoffs from the lower envelope localize the equation; signed bounded expansions occur in a larger Hermitian background.

groups.title: Addition with ordinary type or bounded carrier
groups.source_reader_scope: The four-step construction distinguishes the minimal ordinary type, phi ordinary type, one ordinary-type input, and a bounded carrier. Cancellation on stretch contact sets, disjoint rooftop partition, first-moment control and fixed finite domination provide common lower bounds. Scaling preserves backgrounds/classes and returns any positive exponent.

groups.title: Model equations and reference stability
groups.source_reader_scope: Maximize a finite weighted measure between nu0 and a carrier-controlled datum. Fixed domination identifies the maximizing equation; addition of a supersolution for the remaining measure forces equality. Increasing density truncation gives arbitrary data. A zero-exponent limit determines a positive scalar; summable density errors plus varying-model closure give total variation and capacity limits, with normalized-potential uniqueness unclaimed at zero.

groups.title: Unrestricted weighted addition and algebra
groups.source_reader_scope: After existence, truncate only exponential weights. A first-moment criterion yields a noncollapsed decreasing limit, and a rooftop of this limit with both inputs gives localization before comparing with the inputs. Strict domination gives a<=u,v. Injectivity of the weighted-measure map yields associativity, translation and the diagonal logarithmic identity, even for infinite weighted mass.

groups.title: Relative boundedness and Lp data
groups.source_reader_scope: The concave envelope is constructed for an arbitrary E_phi potential with bounded slope; local bounded convex compositions glue after decreasing truncation. An m>2n+1 moment bound gives a differential inequality with superlinear W exponent and hence finite depth T. Uniform exponential integrability and Holder provide all finite moments for Lp data. The concluding corollary/proof are byte-exact; only outside-body page enlargement is proposed.
